definition: A pack whose module is a unit of construction rather than a column: most often a unit of material — a brick course, a dressed stone, a log, a light of glass — or of framing, like a structural bay or a storey's height.
more: Most traditional buildings were never proportioned from an order but from a brick course, a joist span or a pane of glass; these packs encode those systems, which are just as parametric.
basis: Our wording of the pack schema's module-system kind and the modules its packs name. schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, kind description: "module-system: a material module governing dimension."; schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, top-level description: "Non-classical packs use the same machinery with a material module (brick course, timber bay, sash light) in place of a column diameter."; proportions/modules/brick-course.json module.name: "One coursing measure: four brick courses, each course being one brick bed-depth plus one bed joint"; proportions/modules/stone-course.json module.name: "One dressed stone: the bed height a banker mason cuts a quoin, jamb or lintel to"; proportions/modules/log-module.json module.name: "One wall log: the length of a hewn or round log that two men can carry"; proportions/modules/sash-light.json module.name: "One light of glass: the largest single pane the period's glasshouse could reliably supply"; proportions/modules/timber-bay.json module.name: "One structural bay: the distance from the centre of one principal cross-frame (bent) to the centre of the next"; proportions/modules/storey-graduation.json module.name: "One storey height of the principal floor, measured floor surface to floor surface"; docs/proportion.md: "Most traditional buildings were never proportioned from an order; they were proportioned from a brick course, a joist span, or a pane of glass."; docs/proportion.md: "Those systems are just as parametric".
